capability.network.observe.title: Observe network traffic
capability.network.observe.definition: Read communication units and exposed transport metadata on a scoped path.
assumptions: The attacker has the stated degree of access to a communication path.
exclusions: This capability does not imply endpoint, key-material, or physical compromise.

capability.network.inject.title: Inject network input
capability.network.inject.definition: Introduce attacker-chosen communication units onto a scoped path.
assumptions: The attacker has the stated degree of access to a communication path.
exclusions: This capability does not imply endpoint, key-material, or physical compromise.

capability.network.modify.title: Modify network input
capability.network.modify.definition: Alter communication units in transit before delivery.
assumptions: The attacker has the stated degree of access to a communication path.
exclusions: This capability does not imply endpoint, key-material, or physical compromise.

capability.network.delete.title: Delete network input
capability.network.delete.definition: Prevent selected communication units from reaching an intended receiver.
assumptions: The attacker has the stated degree of access to a communication path.
exclusions: This capability does not imply endpoint, key-material, or physical compromise.

capability.network.delay.title: Delay network input
capability.network.delay.definition: Hold selected communication units and deliver them later.
assumptions: The attacker has the stated degree of access to a communication path.
exclusions: This capability does not imply endpoint, key-material, or physical compromise.

capability.network.duplicate.title: Duplicate network input
capability.network.duplicate.definition: Deliver additional copies of selected communication units.
assumptions: The attacker has the stated degree of access to a communication path.
exclusions: This capability does not imply endpoint, key-material, or physical compromise.

capability.network.replay.title: Replay captured input
capability.network.replay.definition: Reintroduce a previously observed communication unit.
assumptions: The attacker has the stated degree of access to a communication path.
exclusions: This capability does not imply endpoint, key-material, or physical compromise.

capability.network.reorder.title: Reorder network input
capability.network.reorder.definition: Change the delivery order of selected communication units.
assumptions: The attacker has the stated degree of access to a communication path.
exclusions: This capability does not imply endpoint, key-material, or physical compromise.

capability.participation.authenticated-m.title: Authenticated malicious participation
capability.participation.authenticated-m.definition: Act through a valid participant identity while choosing inputs or state transitions adversarially.
assumptions: The attacker is admitted as an authenticated participant within a bounded context.
exclusions: Authentication does not grant every role, permission, or endpoint capability.

capability.endpoint.read-storage.title: Read endpoint storage
capability.endpoint.read-storage.definition: Read scoped persistent endpoint state and stored material.
assumptions: The attacker has the stated access to one scoped endpoint resource.
exclusions: Access does not imply control of every endpoint, service, or external communication path.

capability.endpoint.read-memory.title: Read endpoint memory
capability.endpoint.read-memory.definition: Read scoped volatile endpoint state and material during operation.
assumptions: The attacker has the stated access to one scoped endpoint resource.
exclusions: Access does not imply control of every endpoint, service, or external communication path.

capability.endpoint.write-state.title: Write endpoint memory or storage
capability.endpoint.write-state.definition: Modify scoped volatile or persistent endpoint state.
assumptions: The attacker has the stated access to one scoped endpoint resource.
exclusions: Access does not imply control of every endpoint, service, or external communication path.

capability.infrastructure.control-interm.title: Control an intermediary
capability.infrastructure.control-interm.definition: Control a scoped intermediary that processes or forwards communication data.
assumptions: The identified intermediary, relay, or service is within the attacker-controlled boundary.
exclusions: Control does not imply compromise of end-to-end protected endpoints unless separately stated.

capability.infrastructure.control-relay.title: Control a relay
capability.infrastructure.control-relay.definition: Control a scoped message relay or delivery component.
assumptions: The identified intermediary, relay, or service is within the attacker-controlled boundary.
exclusions: Control does not imply compromise of end-to-end protected endpoints unless separately stated.

capability.infrastructure.control-servic.title: Control a service
capability.infrastructure.control-servic.definition: Control a scoped service participating in identity, directory, routing, or communication processing.
assumptions: The identified intermediary, relay, or service is within the attacker-controlled boundary.
exclusions: Control does not imply compromise of end-to-end protected endpoints unless separately stated.

capability.secret-compromise.long-term.title: Compromise long-term secret
assumptions: The specified class of secret material is available to the attacker for the scoped period.
exclusions: No other secret class or time period is implicitly compromised.

capability.secret-compromise.session.title: Compromise session secret
capability.secret-compromise.session.definition: Obtain scoped secret material associated with one session.
assumptions: The specified class of secret material is available to the attacker for the scoped period.
exclusions: No other secret class or time period is implicitly compromised.

capability.secret-compromise.ephemeral.title: Compromise ephemeral secret
capability.secret-compromise.ephemeral.definition: Obtain scoped short-lived secret material before its intended destruction.
assumptions: The specified class of secret material is available to the attacker for the scoped period.
exclusions: No other secret class or time period is implicitly compromised.

capability.secret-compromise.derived.title: Compromise derived secret
capability.secret-compromise.derived.definition: Obtain scoped material derived for a particular purpose or context.
assumptions: The specified class of secret material is available to the attacker for the scoped period.
exclusions: No other secret class or time period is implicitly compromised.

capability.time-state.manipulate-clock.title: Manipulate clock input
capability.time-state.manipulate-clock.definition: Influence a scoped clock or time source used for a security decision.
assumptions: The attacker can influence the stated local time or persistent-state input.
exclusions: The capability does not imply arbitrary code execution or access to unrelated state.

capability.time-state.rollback-persisten.title: Rollback persistent state
capability.time-state.rollback-persisten.definition: Replace scoped persistent security state with an earlier valid representation.
assumptions: The attacker can influence the stated local time or persistent-state input.
exclusions: The capability does not imply arbitrary code execution or access to unrelated state.

capability.input-resource.deliver-malfor.title: Deliver malformed input
capability.input-resource.deliver-malfor.definition: Supply syntactically or semantically malformed data to a scoped parser or state machine.
assumptions: The attacker can supply input or consume resources through an exposed interface.
exclusions: The capability does not imply a vulnerability or successful denial of service.

capability.input-resource.exhaust-resour.title: Exhaust bounded resources
capability.input-resource.exhaust-resour.definition: Consume scoped compute, memory, storage, bandwidth, or request capacity.
assumptions: The attacker can supply input or consume resources through an exposed interface.
exclusions: The capability does not imply a vulnerability or successful denial of service.

capability.supply-chain.modify-artifact.title: Modify build or release artifact
capability.supply-chain.modify-artifact.definition: Alter a scoped build input, build output, or release artifact before deployment.
assumptions: The attacker can alter the specified pre-deployment artifact boundary.
exclusions: The capability does not imply control of source history, signing authority, or deployed endpoints unless stated.

capability.observation.traffic-pattern.title: Observe traffic patterns
capability.observation.traffic-pattern.definition: Observe scoped message sizes, timing, frequency, direction, or relationship metadata.
assumptions: The attacker can obtain the stated observable signal.
exclusions: Observation does not imply message plaintext or secret-key access.

capability.observation.side-channel.title: Observe side channel
capability.observation.side-channel.definition: Observe scoped physical or implementation-dependent signals correlated with protected processing.
assumptions: The attacker can obtain the stated observable signal.
exclusions: Observation does not imply message plaintext or secret-key access.

capability.physical.access-device.title: Physical device access
capability.physical.access-device.definition: Interact physically with a scoped device, component, or interface.
assumptions: The attacker can interact physically with the scoped device or environment.
exclusions: Physical access does not automatically imply successful secret extraction or persistent control.

capability.physical.inject-fault.title: Inject physical fault
capability.physical.inject-fault.definition: Induce a scoped abnormal physical or electrical condition during processing.
assumptions: The attacker can interact physically with the scoped device or environment.
exclusions: Physical access does not automatically imply successful secret extraction or persistent control.

attacker.passive-network-observer.title: Passive network observer
attacker.passive-network-observer.definition: Observes a scoped communication path without injecting traffic.
assumptions: The observer can access the identified path or radio/transport exposure.
exclusions: No active network action, endpoint compromise, or secret-material compromise is assumed.

attacker.active-network-controller.title: Active network controller
attacker.active-network-controller.definition: Exercises bounded observation and manipulation of a communication path.
assumptions: The attacker controls delivery on the scoped path.
exclusions: Endpoints and their secret material remain uncompromised unless another model is selected.

attacker.authenticated-malicious-peer.title: Authenticated malicious peer
attacker.authenticated-malicious-peer.definition: Participates with a valid scoped identity while acting adversarially.
assumptions: The attacker has valid participation authority for the evaluated context.
exclusions: The model grants no unrelated administrator, endpoint, or service authority.

attacker.endpoint-state-adversary.title: Endpoint state adversary
attacker.endpoint-state-adversary.definition: Reads or changes scoped endpoint state.
assumptions: One identified endpoint is within the attacker-access boundary.
exclusions: Other endpoints, network paths, and infrastructure are not implicitly compromised.

attacker.compromised-infrastructure.title: Compromised intermediary or service
attacker.compromised-infrastructure.definition: Controls scoped intermediary, relay, or service infrastructure.
assumptions: At least one named infrastructure role is compromised.
exclusions: End-to-end endpoint secrets and identities are not implicitly compromised.

attacker.secret-material-adversary.title: Secret-material adversary
attacker.secret-material-adversary.definition: Obtains one or more explicitly scoped classes of secret material.
assumptions: Each compromised secret class and time window is selected explicitly.
exclusions: Compromise does not extend to unspecified keys, parties, periods, or device control.

attacker.local-physical-adversary.title: Local physical adversary
attacker.local-physical-adversary.definition: Uses physical access, observation, or induced faults against one scoped device.
assumptions: The attacker can physically approach or handle the scoped device or environment.
exclusions: Successful key extraction, persistent control, and other devices are excluded unless separately established.

attacker.supply-chain-adversary.title: Build or release supply-chain adversary
assumptions: The attacker can reach a declared build or release artifact boundary.
exclusions: The model does not grant source-history rewrite, signing authority, or runtime access unless separately stated.
